nodes.label: CLAUDE.md (Product Editor current-state reference)
nodes.rationale: Declared the current-state reference: where a doc and the code disagree the code wins; where a doc and this file disagree this file was more recently verified.

nodes.label: Hard constraints: branch first, no commits on main, check in before shipping
nodes.rationale: main is production because deploy.sh git-pulls main on the server; shared checkout goes stale within minutes; autonomous implement->merge chains (PRs #41-#53) left the user reviewing merges rather than deciding them.
nodes.norm_label: hard constraints: branch first, no commits on main, check in before shipping

nodes.label: Three test harnesses (Jest, DB-free services/tests, DB-backed api/tests)
nodes.rationale: services/tests stay DB-free and mediapipe-free so CI runs them as standalone modules; api/tests need real Postgres+Redis because LayoutCatalogue case-sensitivity is a Postgres collation behaviour sqlite won't reproduce.
nodes.norm_label: three test harnesses (jest, db-free services/tests, db-backed api/tests)

nodes.label: Editor page characterization suite
nodes.rationale: Safety net for splitting page.tsx: pins what the page sends and when, must pass unchanged across split PRs.

nodes.label: Unified server-side render pipeline (v1.8)
nodes.rationale: Client-side <=20 canvas shortcut removed; every Submit/Download is a Celery job. Trade-off: +10-20s latency on small jobs for one contract covering webhooks, large batches and resumable uploads.

nodes.label: Access-mode invariant (dashboard vs embed produce identical print)
nodes.rationale: Authentication and delivery differ between dashboard and iframe, but editor state, render behaviour and the download artifact contract must not.
nodes.norm_label: access-mode invariant (dashboard vs embed produce identical print)

nodes.label: Shared Render Submission Service (RenderSubmissionService)
nodes.rationale: PR #133 unified CanvasData upsert, RenderJob creation, queue selection and dispatch for both GenerateLayoutView and EditorRenderView.

nodes.label: Editor page.tsx split into hooks and components
nodes.rationale: page.tsx was the file most likely to break something else; split per LARGE_FILE_SPLIT_PLAN into useServerRender, useDesignPersistence, useFileIntake, useCanvasGeneration, useCardActions, useCalendarEditor, useBookPages etc., keeping hook call order so effect order is unchanged.
nodes.norm_label: editor page.tsx split into hooks and components

nodes.label: Scalar API reference and drf-spectacular schema rules
nodes.rationale: A view without @extend_schema is dropped from the schema; SECURITY_DEFINITIONS is a drf-yasg name silently ignored; AllowAny views that gate writes in-handler need explicit per-operation auth= or the reference advertises destructive methods as public.
nodes.norm_label: scalar api reference and drf-spectacular schema rules

nodes.label: Single Celery worker draining priority+standard queues
nodes.rationale: The priority worker never executed a task after CMYK was retired and was removed; the survivor drains both queues as a safety net (not QoS) so an apply_async(queue='priority') can't sit in Redis forever.
nodes.norm_label: single celery worker draining priority+standard queues

nodes.label: GC health: stale vs failing on /api/celery/monitor/
nodes.rationale: is_deleted counts read 0 whether the GC ran or not; stale means no successful sweep, failing means the last attempt raised. Recording only successes let a wrong diagnosis run two days in 2026-08-14. Kept off /api/health so a stale GC can't restart containers.
nodes.norm_label: gc health: stale vs failing on /api/celery/monitor/

nodes.label: GC runs every 6 hours, not nightly
nodes.rationale: Exports expire in a 03:00-12:00 UTC wave; a 02:00 sweep collected 2% and effective retention became ~4 days with disk sawtoothing 82->93% while the sweep itself was healthy.
nodes.norm_label: gc runs every 6 hours, not nightly

nodes.label: Celery stale DB connection hardening
nodes.rationale: CONN_MAX_AGE does nothing in a worker (no request signals); close_old_connections on task_prerun/postrun plus CONN_HEALTH_CHECKS. Hardening, not a fix for an observed incident.

nodes.label: Orphaned export directory sweep (GC_ORPHAN_SWEEP)
nodes.rationale: The one sweep that deletes on absence of evidence, so it defaults to dry_run; five conditions must hold in _classify; a DB failure keeps everything.

nodes.label: Abandoned chunk-upload staging sweep
nodes.rationale: Deletes by default unlike orphan_exports because .part fragments are unusable without /complete; uses newest mtime of contents so a slow live upload is never a candidate. Briefly duplicated an inline block in garbage_collector_task.

nodes.label: Layouts load from Postgres LayoutCatalogue, not disk
nodes.rationale: LayoutEngine must receive layout_definition or render fails with Errno 2; moving identity into the DB removed git-sync divergence and Mac/Linux case-sensitivity bugs.
nodes.norm_label: layouts load from postgres layoutcatalogue, not disk

nodes.label: Chunked upload API (/upload/init, chunk, complete)
nodes.rationale: 2 MB chunks, 4 parallel, UUID v4 guard against path traversal, 50 MB per-file limit, PIL integrity check on assemble.

nodes.label: Embed session and order_id/callback_url header flow
nodes.rationale: order_id and callback_url never appear in the iframe URL: caller -> session DB -> proxy cache -> X-Order-ID/X-Callback-URL headers -> Django. Anything injected as a header must be in the cached tuple.
nodes.norm_label: embed session and order_id/callback_url header flow

nodes.label: Signed completion webhook payload
nodes.rationale: download_url is the combined archive; print/mock/uploads URLs are the same job split by ?content=; HMAC-SHA256 of api_key in X-Signature; no domain allowlist because the api_key already authenticates the caller.

nodes.label: Embed proxy allowlist (path AND method, fail-closed)
nodes.rationale: Checked before token resolution so a stolen token can't probe Django auth. The method half is load-bearing: the proxy injects the session's real (ops-flagged) api_key, so a GET-only prefix without method enforcement let an embed token PUT holiday data until 2026-09-03.
nodes.norm_label: embed proxy allowlist (path and method, fail-closed)

nodes.label: HEIC decoding chain (heic2any -> browser codec -> server pillow-heif)
nodes.rationale: iOS 18 gain-map HEICs defeat heic2any (last published 2021) and Chrome/Firefox have no HEIC codec, so the server decoder is the only universal path. It preserves ICC and writes no EXIF to avoid double rotation.
nodes.norm_label: heic decoding chain (heic2any -> browser codec -> server pillow-heif)

nodes.label: Order quantity (qty) rule: hard cap over, warn under
nodes.rationale: Under-upload must never block: a wrong caller-supplied qty would strand a real order. Server looks qty up from EmbedSession, never the header, after a direct POST bypassed the cap (2026-09-15). Server half is narrower and fails open so it can never 400 what the editor allowed.
nodes.norm_label: order quantity (qty) rule: hard cap over, warn under

nodes.label: postMessage contract (pe:render_job, pe:back) with locked targetOrigin
nodes.rationale: pe:back exists because an iframe shares the tab's joint session history, so history.back() can carry the customer off printo.in mid-checkout. targetOrigin resolves ancestorOrigins -> referrer -> env -> https://printo.in, never '*'.
nodes.norm_label: postmessage contract (pe:render_job, pe:back) with locked targetorigin

nodes.label: Auth & login flow (NextAuth v5 + PIA)
nodes.rationale: authorize() separates bad credentials (4xx -> null) from PIA outage (5xx/timeout -> typed errors) so users don't retype passwords during an incident; Google sign-in is just another way to obtain PIA tokens, gated to @printo.in server-side.

nodes.label: Three frame renderers - the drift trap
nodes.rationale: Anything drawn inside a frame exists in FabricEditor (live), fabric-renderer (thumbnail) and engine.py (print); frame-fill.ts and caption-layout parity tests exist to stop drift.
nodes.norm_label: three frame renderers - the drift trap

nodes.label: TS<->Python parity test pattern
nodes.rationale: Shared fixtures under storage/parity-fixtures pin calendar grid, calendar year, holiday gate, caption layout, shape catalogue, book layout and the qty rule across the language boundary.

nodes.label: Layout identity: immutable name vs ops-editable display_name
nodes.rationale: name is hardcoded by printo.in into embed URLs, so renames silently 404'd their embed; renaming was retired, display_name added, and the renamed_to alias kept as a safety net for the one pre-fix rename.
nodes.norm_label: layout identity: immutable name vs ops-editable display_name

nodes.label: Brand colours: Tailwind indigo overridden to Printo purple
nodes.rationale: Overriding the indigo scale re-skinned every call site at once instead of touching hundreds; don't fix a class back to hex or add a second purple scale.
nodes.norm_label: brand colours: tailwind indigo overridden to printo purple

nodes.label: Prod runs STORAGE_BACKEND=s3 (masks, fonts, calendar assets, stickers)
nodes.rationale: Code defaults to local but prod is S3; seeds are only defaults for keys S3 never held; deletes write tombstones and outages raise CalendarAssetUnavailable rather than resurrecting seeds; masks print from S3 via _load_mask.
nodes.norm_label: prod runs storage_backend=s3 (masks, fonts, calendar assets, stickers)

nodes.label: Mask and sticker previews via CloudFront CDN
nodes.rationale: Content-fingerprinted filenames mean no invalidation is needed; the shared pia-oms-uploads bucket policy is edited by adding statements, never replacing.
nodes.norm_label: mask and sticker previews via cloudfront cdn

nodes.label: Backups (backup.sh / restore.sh / test-backup-restore.sh)
nodes.rationale: Scheduled 03:15 UTC since 2026-08-28; archives S3 ops-config too; weekly tier is PII-free so customer data lives at most 7 days in backups.

nodes.label: Layout templates (ops-authored decoration)
nodes.rationale: Decoration lives on the customer's cards, not in the render path, so the print needs no new step; a template never holds a customer file; a restored design wins over the URL's template id.

nodes.label: Calendar product type (materialize 12 surfaces)
nodes.rationale: One template expands to 12 per-month surfaces at render time; per-day entries anchor to ISO dates so type flips never misplace them; photo i maps to month i mod N.

nodes.label: Book / photobook product type (materialize pages)
nodes.rationale: Mirrors the calendar's materialize architecture, not its renderer; page count is customer state snapped up to the step grid; gutter mirrored by parity; spine width counts leaves not sides (unconfirmed with Catalog Ops).

nodes.label: Auto-orientation: rotate-to-fill first, MediaPipe Pose second
nodes.rationale: Ops decision 2026-05-19: filling the frame beats keeping people upright. Inline endpoint rather than Celery because generateCanvases needs the rotation before drawing the preview.
nodes.norm_label: auto-orientation: rotate-to-fill first, mediapipe pose second

nodes.label: Service Worker (cache-first for hashed static assets)
nodes.rationale: Production-only registration so dev changes always hit the network; never caches HTML or auth-gated responses.
nodes.norm_label: service worker (cache-first for hashed static assets)

nodes.label: Never-lose-edits (canvas reuse by file identity)
nodes.rationale: canvas-merge plans reuse by name:size:lastModified not grid position; lost photos and lost local images block submit and are named rather than silently dropped from the print.

nodes.label: Autosave never writes before the restore lands (restoreSettled)
nodes.rationale: Autosave deliberately writes empty state, so a PUT during the restore GET wipes the saved design; gate on restoreSettled not restorePending (which the embed never sets). Chrome masks the race by holding same-URL PUTs.
nodes.norm_label: autosave never writes before the restore lands (restoresettled)

nodes.label: SSRF protection for callback URLs
nodes.rationale: validate_public_https_url at session-create and post_webhook_safely at send time, pinning the socket to the validated IP so DNS can't rebind; never requests.post a customer callback_url directly.

nodes.label: DPDP order data purge
nodes.rationale: Hard-deletes rows and files; key-scoped by default because order ids are unique only per key - a key-scoped purge used to delete another key's photos (fixed 2026-10-07).

nodes.label: Purge ledger (HMAC'd erasures replayed after restore)
nodes.rationale: Lives outside Postgres so a restore cannot roll it back; restore.sh runs reapply_purges so a restored dump re-erases orders purged after it.
nodes.norm_label: purge ledger (hmac'd erasures replayed after restore)

nodes.label: editor_state vs render_state ownership contract
nodes.rationale: editor_state is written only by autosave (CanvasStateView); render_state only by EditorRenderView at submit and read by render_canvas_task - so submit never wipes the saved design and autosave can't strip a queued job.

nodes.label: API audit trail (APIRequest rows)
nodes.rationale: Table existed with nothing writing to it, so count 0 read as proof a key was never used; high-frequency endpoints exempt; the write can never break a request; jobs_per_day comes from here, not RenderJob.

nodes.label: Deployment via deploy.sh (nginx inode trap, entrypoint ignores $@, build-time collectstatic)
nodes.rationale: nginx.conf is a single-file bind mount binding the inode, so a changed config needs the proxy recreated, not reloaded; entrypoint.sh always runs migrate+gunicorn; collectstatic needs an inline build-only DJANGO_SECRET_KEY.
nodes.norm_label: deployment via deploy.sh (nginx inode trap, entrypoint ignores $@, build-time collectstatic)

nodes.label: Observability owned outside this repo (Sentry + container logs only)
nodes.rationale: Grafana/Loki removed 2026-09-07 because the server lead owns monitoring; json-file logs at 50 MB x 3 are lost on container recreation; never put the prod SENTRY_DSN in a local .env.
nodes.norm_label: observability owned outside this repo (sentry + container logs only)

nodes.label: Role model: Admin (is_staff) / Ops (is_ops_team) / Editor
nodes.rationale: Rules live in lib/roles.ts so the badge can never claim a privilege a gate refuses; reverses PR #24; reads stay open because GET ops/layouts feeds the Editor tier.

nodes.label: Ops privilege gate must live in the internal proxy
nodes.rationale: Everything through the internal proxy presents the shared ops-flagged INTERNAL_API_KEY, so Django's IsOpsTeam sees one identity; only the proxy knows the human. Views mounted twice need OPS_OWNED_PATHS plus READ_ONLY public routes.
nodes.norm_label: ops privilege gate must live in the internal proxy

nodes.label: Django admin SSO via nginx auth_request + signed identity headers
nodes.rationale: HMAC with a purpose-bound key derived from EMBED_INTERNAL_SECRET stops anything on the Docker network minting itself is_superuser; flags are asserted every request from PIA.
nodes.norm_label: django admin sso via nginx auth_request + signed identity headers

nodes.label: P1 fix: autosave payload bloat (strip base64 previews)
nodes.rationale: 37% of canvas-state PUTs were 400s on the 10 MB limit; fixed by not persisting previews rather than raising the limit, which would trade silent failures for OOM on a 2-core box.
nodes.norm_label: p1 fix: autosave payload bloat (strip base64 previews)

nodes.label: Overlay print/preview drift fix (2026-10-13)
nodes.rationale: fontSize is print px and was wrongly scaled by canvas height/800; wrapping now follows Fabric's algorithm; shapes draw from the shape_catalog twin with Fabric's placement.

nodes.label: Overlay fonts are Google Fonts only; ops retire rather than delete
nodes.rationale: Print allows active plus retired fonts so a design never loses the font it was made with; FontUnavailable fails the job rather than printing a listed font in another.
nodes.norm_label: overlay fonts are google fonts only; ops retire rather than delete

nodes.label: image_loader.open_source_rgba is the single choke point for customer photos
nodes.rationale: EXIF orientation plus ICC->sRGB via lcms2; Image.open().convert('RGBA') silently discards the embedded profile and shifts print colours.
nodes.norm_label: image_loader.open_source_rgba is the single choke point for customer photos

nodes.label: Knowledge graph maintenance (graphify-refresh.py, not graphify update)
nodes.rationale: graphify update re-adds per-heading doc nodes and unnames communities; builds from a scratchpad worktree bake its path into IDs; read counts from GRAPH_REPORT.md.
nodes.norm_label: knowledge graph maintenance (graphify-refresh.py, not graphify update)

nodes.label: Calendar Feature PRD
nodes.author: Kanna
nodes.rationale: Historical design record for the v1.12 foundation (server-side overlays) and v1.13 calendar product; where it disagrees with code, code wins. Two things shipped differently: cells are one flat ISO-date map, and photo canvases are capped at 12 with month i using photo (i mod N).

nodes.label: Calendar primitive (layout-agnostic positioned region)
nodes.rationale: A {x,y,width,height}-percent region inside any canvas owning only grid, cells, pills, holidays and per-cell editing; frames and artwork stay with the layout, so desk, full-page, poster and side-by-side calendars come free via layout authoring. Layout-authored, customer-overridden.

nodes.label: Minimal customer-facing controls principle
nodes.rationale: Every knob is a chance for an off-brand print; 'templates, not configurators' costs less to maintain, produces fewer support tickets and protects print quality. Font, grid, week-start and position stay ops-locked; customer gets theme, Gen-Z palette, calendar type and cell contents.

nodes.label: Overlays preview-only gap (server drew no text/shape/image)
nodes.rationale: engine.py had zero ImageDraw/ImageFont imports, so TextOverlay/ShapeOverlay/ImageOverlay appeared in thumbnails and vanished from the printed PNG/PDF. Pre-existing and unrelated to calendars, but a hard prerequisite for shipping one.
nodes.norm_label: overlays preview-only gap (server drew no text/shape/image)

nodes.label: Phase 1 Server-side overlay rendering (v1.12)
nodes.rationale: Built as services/overlay_renderer.py (render_overlays) plus services/fonts.py, wired into _composite_canvas after frame compositing and before the paper mask. Ships on its own and unblocks every existing overlay type, not just the calendar.

nodes.label: ISO-date keyed cell entries (flat product-wide map)
nodes.rationale: Shipped as one flat { iso_date: [CellOverride] } map instead of the 12-slot cellsPerCanvas array, so photo-canvas count changes and English/Financial flips can never lose or misplace entries; legacy 12-slot arrays are still read on restore.
nodes.norm_label: iso-date keyed cell entries (flat product-wide map)

nodes.label: Photo to month mapping (month i uses photo i mod N, cap 12)
nodes.rationale: Frontend caps photo canvases at 12 and the engine renders exactly 12 outputs; one photo cycles to every month, 12 map one-per-month, so upload order matters. An earlier build produced 12·N files in the ZIP.
nodes.norm_label: photo to month mapping (month i uses photo i mod n, cap 12)

nodes.label: Calendar grid rendering algorithm (identical client/server math)
nodes.rationale: firstCellOffset, totalCells (28/35/42), cellW/cellH, weekday header, per-cell override drawing, grid lines — computed the same way in lib/calendar.ts and calendar_renderer.py so preview matches print.
nodes.norm_label: calendar grid rendering algorithm (identical client/server math)

nodes.label: Calendar z-order slot (above overlays, below mask)
nodes.norm_label: calendar z-order slot (above overlays, below mask)

nodes.label: Auto-fit text via ImageFont.getbbox binary search
nodes.rationale: No library fits either side: DOM auto-fit libraries measure via getBoundingClientRect and cannot see a Fabric canvas; Pillow has no fitting helper. ~15 LOC binary search over getbbox is the documented community pattern.
nodes.norm_label: auto-fit text via imagefont.getbbox binary search

nodes.label: Cell images reuse smart-crop + MediaPipe auto-orientation
nodes.rationale: Each cell is a tiny frameSpec, so calculateSmartCropOffsets (client) and the _composite_canvas cover-fit math (server) apply unchanged, and the v1.11 pose pipeline already corrects sideways uploads — zero new cropping or orientation logic.
nodes.norm_label: cell images reuse smart-crop + mediapipe auto-orientation

nodes.label: Pill-style cell entries with rotating 3-slot dotCycle
nodes.rationale: Date number always visible; entries stack as pills with one theme-wide background and a dot colour rotating by entry index, so multi-entry cells stay distinguishable without exposing a colour picker (per the minimal-controls principle).
nodes.norm_label: pill-style cell entries with rotating 3-slot dotcycle

nodes.label: Global holiday auto-load (holidaySource)
nodes.rationale: storage/holidays/<locale>/<year>.json seeded for en-IN and generic × 2026–2030; layout opts in via calendar.holidaySource {enabled, locale}. showInCells shipped as a checkbox nothing read and was removed 2026-09-29.

nodes.label: Nager.Date holiday source
nodes.rationale: Chosen as the seed source at PRD time; later found to have no India coverage (HTTP 204) and replaced by the offline holidays package behind manage.py refresh_holidays.

nodes.label: Three style presets (modern-minimalist, modern-genz, weekday-highlight)
nodes.rationale: Stored as JSON under storage/calendar_styles/; ops picks one when authoring, its style block is copied into the layout. weekday-highlight says one thing — Sundays are different (#FEE2E2 fill, #DC2626 number).
nodes.community_name: Calendar Assets on S3 (Fake S3 Tests) (2)

nodes.label: Gen-Z palettes (Butter & Purple, Mint & Hot Pink, Lilac & Coral, Sky & Lemon)
nodes.rationale: Each palette sets all six colour roles together plus a 3-slot dotCycle; the swatch is the only Gen-Z customisation control. New palettes ship as JSON files under storage/calendar_palettes/genz/ with no code change.
nodes.community_name: Calendar Assets on S3 (Fake S3 Tests) (2)
nodes.norm_label: gen-z palettes (butter & purple, mint & hot pink, lilac & coral, sky & lemon)

nodes.label: Calendar as Multi-Surface Product (productType: calendar)
nodes.rationale: A separate product category would fork render, ops and preview pipelines; pure multi-surface would force ops to hand-build 12 surfaces and keep theme/type in sync. A productType tag on existing multi-surface plumbing (per-surface dispatch, N-file ZIP, single webhook) is the whole architectural cost.

nodes.label: Single-template authoring + 12-surface auto-gen
nodes.rationale: Ops designs one representative month; the layout stores that template and materialize_surfaces expands it into 12 surfaces at render time, only (year, month) varying unless a surfaceOverride says otherwise.

nodes.label: Surface index to (year, month) resolution formula
nodes.rationale: totalOffset = surfaceIndex + (monthOffset ?? 0); realMonth = ((startMonth-1+totalOffset) % 12)+1; realYear = baseYear + floor((startMonth-1+totalOffset)/12). Handles both 12×1 and 1×12 modes uniformly.
nodes.norm_label: surface index to (year, month) resolution formula

nodes.label: Per-surface overrides (surfaceOverrides, field-level replace)
nodes.rationale: Sparse map keyed month_ii; effective(surface) = template ⊕ override. Fields replace rather than deep-merge because merging arrays (by id? concatenate? positional?) is ambiguous and every interpretation leaks to UX. frames, calendar position and overlays may be overridden; canvas, themePreset, calendarType, weekStart may not.

nodes.label: Auto-rolling year (defaultYear: current)
nodes.rationale: Resolved at editor mount so layouts never freeze to a year and need no ops intervention each January; Financial type uses the previous calendar year as base when today is Jan–Mar. Shipped as resolveDefaultYear / resolve_default_year with a parity fixture.

nodes.label: English vs Financial calendar type (startMonth 1 vs 4)
nodes.norm_label: english vs financial calendar type (startmonth 1 vs 4)

nodes.label: productType as extension point (photobook etc.)
nodes.rationale: Multi-surface is the generic substrate for 'designed once, replicated N times with per-instance data'; each productType gets its own ops and preview UIs while storage and render layers are shared. Photobook was named as the next candidate and became the Book PRD.

nodes.label: calendars[] plural primitives (multi-surface vs poster mode)
nodes.rationale: count=12 × 1 calendar (desk/wall) or count=1 × 12 calendars with monthOffset (year-on-one-poster); validator enforces monthRange.count × calendars.length === 12.
nodes.norm_label: calendars[] plural primitives (multi-surface vs poster mode)

nodes.label: Cell-image expiry re-upload prompt
nodes.rationale: Cell images follow the UploadedFile GC; a GC'd image renders blank with an inline 'Image expired — please re-upload' prompt rather than any automatic recovery.

nodes.label: Calendar type flip warning modal
nodes.rationale: Entries outside the new 12-month range are hidden, not deleted — they stay keyed by ISO date and re-render if the customer flips back.

nodes.label: Fail-all-or-nothing multi-surface render failure
nodes.rationale: If 1 of N surfaces fails the whole RenderJob fails, partial outputs are cleaned up and the error names the month; retry re-renders all N. Per-surface retry deferred to v2.

nodes.label: Single bundled font Inter Variable, no picker (§11.7, reversed 2026-10-13)
nodes.rationale: Original rule: one bundled Inter-Variable.ttf for all text so preview and print cannot drift and 'font missing' cannot happen. Reversed 2026-10-13 for text overlays, which now print in the chosen Google font via services/google_fonts.py; Inter remains the default and the calendar grid font.
nodes.norm_label: single bundled font inter variable, no picker (§11.7, reversed 2026-10-13)

nodes.label: Feb 29 entries on non-leap years (hidden, toast)
nodes.norm_label: feb 29 entries on non-leap years (hidden, toast)

nodes.label: Hard cap of 3 entries per cell, no overflow badge
nodes.norm_label: hard cap of 3 entries per cell, no overflow badge

nodes.label: User-first MAX_ENTRIES precedence
nodes.rationale: User entries fill the 3 slots first, holidays take what remains, overflow is silently suppressed. Reverses the original holidays-first rule: customer intent beats auto-injection.

nodes.label: Validator rejects banned surfaceOverrides fields
nodes.rationale: banned = {themePreset, calendarType, weekStart, canvas, monthRange}; 400 names the field so manual JSON edits cannot bypass the layout-global rule.

nodes.label: IST-only renderer timezone with ISO date strings
nodes.rationale: The renderer never calls datetime.now(); 'today' is computed client-side in Asia/Kolkata only for year derivation. All v1 customers are in India.
nodes.norm_label: ist-only renderer timezone with iso date strings

nodes.label: No layout versioning — fresh load per embed
nodes.rationale: Each session loads the current layout; acceptable because calendar sessions are short and ops rarely edits published layouts. Add layoutVersion and lock active orders if edit frequency rises.
nodes.norm_label: no layout versioning — fresh load per embed

nodes.label: v2 readiness — S3 signed-URL download path
nodes.rationale: The Next.js proxy buffers whole ZIPs (300 MB peak); v2 would redirect RenderJobDownloadView to a signed S3 URL with the same webhook field names. v1 rule: all output goes through the EXPORTS_DIR abstraction, no hardcoded disk paths.
nodes.norm_label: v2 readiness — s3 signed-url download path

nodes.label: Zero DB migrations — JSON in existing free-form columns
nodes.rationale: Calendar template rides in layout JSON and customer state in CanvasData.editor_state, both free-form, so old states deserialise cleanly and no schema migration was needed.
nodes.norm_label: zero db migrations — json in existing free-form columns

nodes.label: Ops vs customer control split (theme, palette, calendar type customer-controllable)
nodes.norm_label: ops vs customer control split (theme, palette, calendar type customer-controllable)

nodes.label: Out-of-month cells show date number only
nodes.rationale: Filler cells render greyed in outOfMonthColor with no entries, pills or images — avoids 'is this entry for this month or the next?' ambiguity.
nodes.norm_label: out-of-month cells show date number only

nodes.label: TS-Python calendar parity fixtures
nodes.rationale: Shared ground-truth fixtures so any drift between lib/calendar.ts and calendar_renderer.py fails CI on both sides.

nodes.label: Mobile cell editing as bottom sheet
nodes.rationale: 42 tiny tap targets on a phone is painful; the cell editor opens as a list in a bottom sheet below the md breakpoint instead of on the canvas.
nodes.norm_label: mobile cell editing as bottom sheet

nodes.label: Book / Booklet / Photobook Layout PRD
nodes.author: Kanna Perumal
nodes.rationale: 'Book' means any bound page-ordered product. Status at writing: Phases 0–4 built backend-only; decisions D1–D7 all answered 2026-08-14. Deliberately mirrors the calendar PRD's materialize architecture.

nodes.label: productType: book (third product type)
nodes.rationale: Reuse the calendar's materialize architecture, not its renderer: expanding one template into N page-surfaces is structurally the same problem as 12 month-surfaces, while month-grid drawing is irrelevant to a page of frames.

nodes.label: Separate book creator UI
nodes.rationale: Page count is customer-variable, pages come in ordered pairs and the author thinks in spreads — a different mental model, hence its own route like /editor/layouts/calendar/[name].

nodes.label: D1 Flat page list (one entry per printed side)
nodes.rationale: Renderer, ZIP contract and canvases_meta all speak 'one surface, one file'; sheet pairing is an imposition concern. Deriving spreads for preview is cheap; deriving pages from sheets for the renderer would be a permanent tax.
nodes.norm_label: d1 flat page list (one entry per printed side)

nodes.label: D2 Customer-entered page count within range
nodes.rationale: Template declares pageCount {min,max,step,default}; books step in multiples of 4 because of signature folds. Covers sit outside the count and are addressed by role so a count change cannot renumber them. First product where surface count is customer state.
nodes.norm_label: d2 customer-entered page count within range

nodes.label: D2a Exactly two authored templates (cover + innerPage)
nodes.rationale: The author lays out 'an inner page', not page 7; the materializer stamps it N times. Narrower than a roles map; pageOverrides remains the escape hatch for a bespoke page.
nodes.norm_label: d2a exactly two authored templates (cover + innerpage)

nodes.label: D3 Photo to page auto-flow (warn-and-proceed)
nodes.rationale: Flow in upload order one photo per frame; short-fill leaves genuinely blank pages (people leave pages for writing); overflow warns and offers to extend to the next valid count, never blocks — consistent with submit-guards.ts.

nodes.label: D4 Covers authored separately, addressed by role
nodes.rationale: Front and back covers are always present, outside the page count, entries in the one ordered list with role cover/backCover so the renderer and ZIP contract stay 'one surface, one file'.
nodes.norm_label: d4 covers authored separately, addressed by role

nodes.label: Spine width formula (computed from page count)
nodes.rationale: Recomputed on every page-count change, resolved on cover surfaces only. Implemented as (pageCount/2 leaves × paperThicknessMm) + 2 × coverThicknessMm, which differs from this PRD's pageCount × paperThicknessMm sketch (double-counts sides as sheets). Which convention Catalog Ops means is unconfirmed — sign off against a printed sample before any cover ships.
nodes.norm_label: spine width formula (computed from page count)

nodes.label: D7 Per-role canvas size
nodes.rationale: A hardcover wrap is larger than the block it binds; each of cover/innerPage/backCover carries its own canvas block (backCover may inherit the cover's). Costs nothing at the engine because _generate_for_surface already reads canvas per surface; an oversizeMm delta can be UI sugar later.

nodes.label: D5 Gutter mirroring by page parity (gutterMm)
nodes.rationale: One gutterMm figure; odd pages bind left, even right, because a single inner template is stamped on both sides of every spread. Shift is half the gutter, uniform across a page's frames and overlays and capped by the tightest element's headroom so a collage moves together. Covers never shift.
nodes.norm_label: d5 gutter mirroring by page parity (guttermm)

nodes.label: D6 Edit single pages, preview spreads
nodes.rationale: Spreads read like the real book but double canvas width and complicate per-frame editing; single pages reuse the canvas-card grid. pages_to_spreads groups page 1 alone, then facing pairs, trailing verso alone, covers alone.
nodes.norm_label: d6 edit single pages, preview spreads

nodes.label: Book schema sketch (book.cover/innerPage/backCover, pageCount, gutterMm, paperThicknessMm)
nodes.norm_label: book schema sketch (book.cover/innerpage/backcover, pagecount, guttermm, paperthicknessmm)

nodes.label: Collage vs single-photo pages need no schema flag
nodes.rationale: An inner template with one frame is a single-photo page, with N frames a collage; the materializer stamps whatever frame set it is given and the renderer already composites N frames per surface.
nodes.norm_label: collage vs single-photo pages need no schema flag

nodes.label: Prerequisite: multi-photo surface allocation fix
nodes.rationale: Until 2026-08-14 the editor allocated exactly one photo per surface regardless of frame count, so a collage page would have printed the same photo in every cell. Fixed in surface-allocation.ts; never re-introduce a one-photo-per-surface assumption.

nodes.label: Hold per-page overrides when page count lowers
nodes.rationale: Keep overrides on removed pages and restore them if the count goes back up — mirrors how the calendar keeps Feb 29 entries through a non-leap year.
nodes.norm_label: hold per-page overrides when page count lowers

nodes.label: R1 Customer-variable surface count
nodes.rationale: Autosave, restore and the render payload all assumed a fixed surface set; extend canvas-merge.ts identity reuse to pages. Open on the frontend when this PRD was last updated; since resolved in useBookPages (per CLAUDE.md).

nodes.label: No book_renderer.py — a page is just frames
nodes.rationale: Unlike a calendar, the existing _composite_canvas path already draws a book page; page numbers, if ever needed, are an overlay, not a renderer.
nodes.norm_label: no book_renderer.py — a page is just frames

nodes.label: One ZIP, covers named to sort first (no separate archive part)
nodes.rationale: Zero-padded ordinal + role (01 Front Cover, 02 Page 01, …) makes alphabetical order the collation order; no partner webhook payload change needed.
nodes.norm_label: one zip, covers named to sort first (no separate archive part)

nodes.label: Three frame renderers constraint
nodes.rationale: Any new page-level drawing must land in FabricEditor, fabric-renderer and engine.py or go into a shared module such as frame-fill.ts; a fourth parallel renderer is a named risk.

nodes.label: TS-Python parity test pattern for book geometry
nodes.norm_label: ts-python parity test pattern for book geometry

nodes.label: GenerateLayoutView refuses books (needs canvases_meta)
nodes.rationale: The direct partner sync endpoint never builds canvases_meta, so a book would flood every page with the whole photo list; it raises instead. Books submit through POST /api/editor/render only.

nodes.label: Calendar S3-Readiness Audit
nodes.rationale: Phase 9 audit (PRD §11.17), 2026-05-24, amended four times: the 'no hardcoded paths' conclusion held but reads bypassed S3 until 2026-09-29; production has run STORAGE_BACKEND=s3 since 2026-09-04; the transition-path section is historical.

nodes.label: STORAGE_ROOT-derived storage paths
nodes.rationale: One env var; LAYOUTS_DIR (legacy — layouts now in Postgres), EXPORTS_DIR and UPLOADS_DIR derive from it.

nodes.label: Calendar asset paths (palettes, styles, holidays, fonts.json)
nodes.rationale: Font .ttf files ship with the image under services/fonts_assets/, not STORAGE_ROOT — immutable assets, deliberately.
nodes.norm_label: calendar asset paths (palettes, styles, holidays, fonts.json)

nodes.label: S3 calendar asset key mismatch (missing prefix/.json)
nodes.rationale: read_calendar_asset built a key with neither S3_PREFIX nor the .json suffix write_calendar_asset adds, and render-time readers opened STORAGE_ROOT directly, so under S3 every read fell back to local disk and an ops edit reached neither preview nor print. Fixed by routing all readers through asset_store and sharing one key via _calendar_asset_key. Live on prod but no edit had been lost (zero writes in the audit trail).
nodes.norm_label: s3 calendar asset key mismatch (missing prefix/.json)

nodes.label: Tombstone deletes for calendar assets
nodes.rationale: A removed S3 key read as 'never written' and resurrected the git seed; a delete now leaves a tombstone object so only a key S3 has never held reaches the seed.

nodes.label: Fail-closed S3 reads (CalendarAssetUnavailable)
nodes.rationale: Any S3 failure other than NoSuchKey/AccessDenied raises instead of serving the seed: 503 in the preview, a retried render in the print — never a quietly wrong calendar.

nodes.label: Git-seeded local files as S3 default
nodes.norm_label: git-seeded local files as s3 default

nodes.label: refresh_holidays command + offline holidays package
nodes.rationale: scripts/refresh-holidays.py wrote local disk only (under S3 it merged into and rewrote the stale seed) and used Nager.Date, which has no India data; replaced by manage.py refresh_holidays reading and writing through storage from the offline holidays package.

nodes.label: Local-filesystem atomic writes (tempfile + os.replace)
nodes.source_location: Engine output paths, ZIP delivery, S3 transition path
nodes.rationale: The single concrete-storage assumption: engine PNG/PDF output and ZIP building stage a tempfile in the destination dir then os.replace. S3 PutObject is already atomic, so these would become temp → upload → delete.

nodes.label: Proposed blob_store.py shim (never built)
nodes.rationale: services/storage.py (S3Storage/LocalStorage) plus services/asset_store.py took that role; layout JSON moved into Postgres so write_layout_json_atomic no longer exists.

nodes.label: Inter-Variable.ttf (bundled default font)
nodes.rationale: The default for calendar grids, captions and any text overlay with no family, a CSS generic, or a name not on the fonts list; the editor draws those as Inter too. Loaded once per worker on first render.

nodes.label: Single bundled font, no picker (PRD §11.7) — reversed 2026-10-13
nodes.rationale: Text overlays now print in the Google font the customer picked from the ops fonts list, fetched on first use and cached in storage by services/google_fonts.py; those fonts are not bundled.
nodes.norm_label: single bundled font, no picker (prd §11.7) — reversed 2026-10-13

nodes.label: Fallback to PIL default bitmap font
nodes.rationale: If Inter is absent the output still ships, with ugly text and a logged warning.
nodes.norm_label: fallback to pil default bitmap font

nodes.label: Boot-time startup_check() for missing font
nodes.rationale: Flags the miss in the Django log so deploys never silently degrade.

nodes.label: SIL Open Font License 1.1
nodes.rationale: Bundling the .ttf in the Docker image and shipping it inside rendered PNGs is explicitly permitted by OFL §1–3.

nodes.label: Durable Google Font cache (font-cache/<slug>/<weight>.ttf)
nodes.source_location: Do NOT add more fonts here
nodes.rationale: S3 on prod, storage/font_cache/ locally; only families on the ops fonts list are fetched.

nodes.label: Keep fonts_assets single-file
nodes.source_location: Do NOT add more fonts here
nodes.rationale: Picker fonts come from Google Fonts at render time, not from this directory, so adding files here would be dead weight the picker never uses.

nodes.label: Append-only baseline log
nodes.rationale: Each entry is a dated snapshot against a commit; never edit an old row to 'correct' it, add a run. Numbers are only comparable on the same machine.

nodes.label: RateLimitMiddleware 200 req/60s per IP
nodes.rationale: RATE_LIMIT = 200 is set that high because a 200-photo calendar legitimately fires ~600 API calls in under a minute. A flood of /api/layouts returning 429 is the limiter working, not a throughput number.

nodes.label: 2026-07-11 c2babbe baseline (health 3859 rps @50, layouts 753 rps @10)
nodes.rationale: ApacheBench keep-alive on the dev Docker stack; /api/health is unthrottled so it is the raw proxy+gunicorn ceiling.

nodes.label: Webhook payload (order_id, job_id, status, four download URLs, expires_at, qty_summary)
nodes.norm_label: webhook payload (order_id, job_id, status, four download urls, expires_at, qty_summary)

nodes.label: X-Signature HMAC-SHA256 verification over raw body
nodes.rationale: The api_key the storefront already holds is the shared secret, so no new credential is needed and no domain allowlist is required; verification must run on raw bytes (express.raw) and use constant-time comparison because a parsed-then-stringified body changes bytes and === is timing-attack vulnerable.
nodes.norm_label: x-signature hmac-sha256 verification over raw body

nodes.label: qty_summary webhook block (ordered_qty, placed_photos, shortfall, customer_acknowledged_shortfall)
nodes.rationale: Counts are server-derived from the submission (a repeated photo counts per placement); only the acknowledgement flag comes from the editor. null for two-sided, calendar, book or no-qty sessions. It is the only guarantee of count a storefront can rely on because under-upload is deliberately never blocked.
nodes.norm_label: qty_summary webhook block (ordered_qty, placed_photos, shortfall, customer_acknowledged_shortfall)

nodes.label: Split download URLs (?content=print|mock|uploads) alongside combined download_url
nodes.rationale: Storefronts that store mock and print in separate fields could fetch each directly instead of unpacking one archive; nothing is duplicated on disk since the split is a ?content= filter over the same files. download_url stays unchanged so existing callers need no migration. mock returns 404 rather than an empty ZIP so a 22-byte archive is never stored against an order.
nodes.norm_label: split download urls (?content=print|mock|uploads) alongside combined download_url

nodes.label: Webhook retry policy (6 attempts, 2^n backoff, 10 s timeout)
nodes.rationale: Handlers must return 2xx fast and download out-of-band; a synchronous ZIP fetch inside the handler trips the 10 s timeout and each retry creates duplicate downstream work.
nodes.norm_label: webhook retry policy (6 attempts, 2^n backoff, 10 s timeout)

nodes.label: ZIP fetch with Bearer api_key (streamed, 30-500 MB)
nodes.norm_label: zip fetch with bearer api_key (streamed, 30-500 mb)

nodes.label: EmbedSession.callback_url (https-only, <= 2000 chars, no domain allowlist)
nodes.rationale: No domain allowlist because auth is already enforced by the api_key plus the HMAC signature; the URL flows session -> embed proxy -> X-Callback-URL header -> CanvasData and is never in the iframe URL.

nodes.label: qty on POST /api/embed/session (replaces ?qty=N URL param)
nodes.rationale: The URL param was browser-editable and nothing server-side honoured it; storing qty on the session and re-deriving it at submit by order_id means the cap holds whether the request came through the iframe or a direct POST to /api/editor/render. Numeric strings and integral floats are accepted because JSON clients lose the int/float distinction; 0 is an error, not unlimited, because it would cap every order at nothing; true is rejected as a caller bug.

nodes.label: Asymmetric qty rule: over-upload blocked twice, under-upload warned only
nodes.rationale: qty comes from the caller, so a hard gate in both directions would let one wrong value strand a real order at checkout; a customer who over-uploads just removes photos. Storefronts needing a guaranteed count must read qty_summary on the webhook.
nodes.norm_label: asymmetric qty rule: over-upload blocked twice, under-upload warned only

nodes.label: template_id on embed session -> ready editor_url
nodes.rationale: The server validates the template is published and resolves its layout so the caller need not know the layout; an unknown/unpublished id fails at the caller's POST with 400; a returning customer's saved design wins over the template in the link.
nodes.norm_label: template_id on embed session -> ready editor_url

nodes.label: template_flow: picker as first step in the embed
nodes.rationale: The dashboard always asks first; the switch is left to printo.in in the embed. Closing the picker equals Start blank; nothing happens when the layout has no templates or the customer returns to a saved design.
nodes.norm_label: template_flow: picker as first step in the embed

nodes.label: Layout name is an immutable embed key; displayName is the cosmetic field
nodes.source_location: The layout identifier in your iframe URL
nodes.rationale: An ops rename used to 404 the storefront's hardcoded iframe URL with no warning short of a customer complaint. First an alias made renames non-breaking, then renaming was removed outright; layouts renamed before the fix still resolve via a permanent alias.
nodes.norm_label: layout name is an immutable embed key; displayname is the cosmetic field

nodes.label: pe:render_job postMessage (UX-only signal)
nodes.source_location: What also fires alongside the webhook
nodes.rationale: Best-effort and for 'preparing your design' UX only; file delivery is the webhook's job. targetOrigin is locked, never '*'.

nodes.label: pe:back postMessage instead of browser history
nodes.rationale: An iframe has no history stack of its own — one joint session history per tab — so history.back() inside the iframe can walk the parent page backward or off printo.in mid-checkout. Handing the parent a signal keeps the decision in the storefront's own flow; a safe no-op until a listener exists.
nodes.norm_label: pe:back postmessage instead of browser history

nodes.label: Core Product Invariant: dashboard and embed render byte-equivalent output
nodes.rationale: Authentication and delivery may differ by access mode but editor state model, server render pipeline and download artifact contract must not; any implementation leaving per-mode render behaviour is incomplete. Restated in CLAUDE.md as the access-mode invariant and remains policy after the refactor shipped.
nodes.norm_label: core product invariant: dashboard and embed render byte-equivalent output

nodes.label: Shared Render Submission Service (CanvasData upsert + RenderJob + on_commit dispatch)
nodes.rationale: GenerateLayoutView and EditorRenderView each built render jobs themselves, duplicating CanvasData upsert, RenderJob creation, queue selection and Celery dispatch; views become thin auth/contract adapters over one DB/job/queue flow. Shipped 2026-09-04 (PR #133).
nodes.norm_label: shared render submission service (canvasdata upsert + renderjob + on_commit dispatch)

nodes.label: Direct Partner API (POST /api/layout/generate, multipart, async-only, no webhook)
nodes.rationale: Kept rather than removed; must never accept callback_url from the request body and always sets callback_url=None so webhooks stay embed-session-only.
nodes.norm_label: direct partner api (post /api/layout/generate, multipart, async-only, no webhook)

nodes.label: Iframe Embed API (session token, embed proxy injects Bearer + X-Order-ID/X-Callback-URL/X-Include-Uploads)
nodes.rationale: The browser holds only a short-lived X-Embed-Token; Django receives the real API key only from the trusted proxy; allowlist is deny-by-default and never includes ops/admin routes.
nodes.norm_label: iframe embed api (session token, embed proxy injects bearer + x-order-id/x-callback-url/x-include-uploads)

nodes.label: Auth matrix: which caller reaches which route
nodes.norm_label: auth matrix: which caller reaches which route

nodes.label: Removal of unreachable GenerateLayoutView._handle_sync() and with_timeout()
nodes.rationale: post() always routed to async after order_id validation, so the sync helper was dead code that made the direct partner API look legacy; with_timeout outlived it unused and was deleted 2026-10-06.
nodes.norm_label: removal of unreachable generatelayoutview._handle_sync() and with_timeout()

nodes.label: Every doc carries a status line (Current / Shipped / Plan)
nodes.rationale: A PRD with no status gets read as a description of the present — CALENDAR_FEATURE_PRD spent a month claiming Proposal for a shipped feature. History is marked superseded rather than rewritten so version tables stay an audit trail.
nodes.norm_label: every doc carries a status line (current / shipped / plan)

nodes.label: Where a doc and the code disagree, the code wins; CLAUDE.md is the current-state reference
nodes.rationale: Docs are not in CI, so nothing checks their claims; most of docs/ is shipped-feature design records kept for the why, not reference.
nodes.norm_label: where a doc and the code disagree, the code wins; claude.md is the current-state reference

nodes.label: Single retention clock: EXPORT_RETENTION_DAYS (default 7, prod 3), expires_at stamped at creation
nodes.rationale: Separate 14-day file and 30-day CanvasData windows disagreed: expires_at promised partners 30 days while the GC deleted at 14, so a day-20 fetch 404'd. Since migration 0012 expiry is stored on the row rather than recomputed at sweep time, so lowering the env var is no longer retroactive; EXPORT_RETENTION_DAYS_UNDER_PRESSURE defaults to the same value so disk pressure cannot shorten a promised expiry.
nodes.norm_label: single retention clock: export_retention_days (default 7, prod 3), expires_at stamped at creation

nodes.label: DELETE /api/ops/orders/<order_id>/purge (on-demand DPDP erasure)
nodes.rationale: Requires ?all_tenants=true or ?api_key=<name> because order ids are unique only per key; ?force=true overrides the in-flight-render guard. An order counts as found if any artifact exists for it (fixed 2026-10-07 — upload-only orders used to answer No data found). Never on the embed-proxy allowlist.

nodes.label: Uploads stored per order: UPLOADS_DIR/<order_id>/
nodes.rationale: Ownership visible in the path lets an all-tenant purge rmtree the directory and erase what is actually on disk, not only what the DB enumerates; a key-scoped purge deletes file-by-file and leaves the folder because it is per order id not per key (it over-reached into another tenant's photos until 2026-10-07).

nodes.label: Post-commit verification sweep (residual_files, residual_dirs, erasure_complete, unlocated_upload_rows)
nodes.rationale: A bare files_deleted: 0 was indistinguishable from success; re-checking every attempted path and retrying once makes a silently failed unlink (permission error, lock) report incomplete.
nodes.norm_label: post-commit verification sweep (residual_files, residual_dirs, erasure_complete, unlocated_upload_rows)

nodes.label: PII-free weekly backup tier (pg_dump --exclude-table-data on PII_TABLES, no uploads/)
nodes.rationale: Erased orders survived in dumps for ~28 days; with the weekly tier holding no customer data, customer data sits in backups at most 7 days (the daily tier). A new customer-content or IP table must be added to PII_TABLES in scripts/backup.sh and test-backup-restore.sh.
nodes.norm_label: pii-free weekly backup tier (pg_dump --exclude-table-data on pii_tables, no uploads/)

nodes.label: Purge ledger (storage/purge_ledger.jsonl, HMAC of order id, replayed by reapply_purges on restore)
nodes.rationale: Kept outside Postgres so a restore cannot roll it back, with no order id in it (HMAC keyed from SECRET_KEY — rotation orphans it). restore.sh runs manage.py reapply_purges --since <dump ts> after pg_restore; entries older than the dump are ignored so a reused order id survives; a failed ledger write never fails the erasure (ledger_recorded: false). Trimmed by GC on PURGE_LEDGER_RETENTION_DAYS (45).
nodes.norm_label: purge ledger (storage/purge_ledger.jsonl, hmac of order id, replayed by reapply_purges on restore)

nodes.label: Audit blind spots are deliberate but load-bearing (AUDIT_EXEMPT_PREFIXES)
nodes.rationale: /api/health, /api/config, /api/render-status/ and chunk PUTs are exempt because render-status alone produced ~1,500 rows/hour; the /complete call that finalises a file is recorded. A new endpoint touching customer data must not match an exemption or the erasure trail gains a silent gap.
nodes.norm_label: audit blind spots are deliberate but load-bearing (audit_exempt_prefixes)

nodes.label: Orphaned export directory sweep (GC_ORPHAN_SWEEP off/dry_run/delete, armed on prod 2026-09-10)
nodes.rationale: The one sweep that deletes on the absence of a DB row, so it shipped disarmed by default and needed a deliberate arm; five independent guards (UUID name, not in live RenderJob/ExportedResult/CanvasData, age > retention + 1 day) must all hold.
nodes.norm_label: orphaned export directory sweep (gc_orphan_sweep off/dry_run/delete, armed on prod 2026-09-10)

nodes.label: EmbedSession GC sweep (rows with expires_at older than 30 days)
nodes.rationale: Rows hold order_id and caller callback_url, low exposure, but growth was unbounded after the 2 h token expiry; shipped in commit 56a2136 and reported as garbage_collector.embed_sessions_deleted.
nodes.norm_label: embedsession gc sweep (rows with expires_at older than 30 days)

nodes.label: Never delete rows by blank order_id
nodes.rationale: order_id='' is the legitimate value for direct partner API uploads, which have no order context; a blank-order_id cleanup would destroy valid current uploads. Legacy and current rows are distinguishable only by created_at relative to the 0011 deploy.
nodes.norm_label: never delete rows by blank order_id

nodes.label: Autosave blanked CanvasData.image_paths every 2 s via update_or_create defaults
nodes.rationale: The browser never sees server paths so the autosave body carries none; CanvasStateView.put wrote image_paths or [] into defaults, so the purge found no files, deleted rows and reported files_deleted: 0 while 6.4 GB of photos stayed on disk across 265 orders. render_state['image_paths'] survived only because migration 0008 separated submit from autosave.
nodes.norm_label: autosave blanked canvasdata.image_paths every 2 s via update_or_create defaults

nodes.label: Option A: write image_paths only when the caller supplies it
nodes.rationale: Stops the bleeding with no migration, but does nothing for rows already blanked or for abandoned uploads; pinned by services/tests/test_erasure_contract.py.
nodes.norm_label: option a: write image_paths only when the caller supplies it

nodes.label: Option B: UploadedFile.order_id linkage recorded at upload (migration 0011)
nodes.rationale: Makes erasure provable — delete every UploadedFile where order_id = X needs no cooperation from canvas state — and reaches abandoned uploads that were never placed in a canvas. Populated from X-Order-ID or the request; direct-API uploads record blank. Backfill (phase 3) waived because the instance was fresh-start reset with 0 rows when 0011 landed.
nodes.norm_label: option b: uploadedfile.order_id linkage recorded at upload (migration 0011)

nodes.label: Option C: filesystem discovery sweep in the purge (viable only after per-order paths)
nodes.rationale: Uploads were stored flat with a random prefix so no path->order mapping existed; without one a sweep either misses files or deletes another order's. Once uploads moved to UPLOADS_DIR/<order_id>/ the purge deletes the directory outright — verified against a file with no UploadedFile row at all. _no_order/ is excluded and keep_paths (shared originals) still wins.
nodes.norm_label: option c: filesystem discovery sweep in the purge (viable only after per-order paths)

nodes.label: order_id '..' matched the identifier regex — path segment needs its own check
nodes.rationale: order_id permits '.', so '..' passed validation and the purge's rmtree would have targeted the parent of the uploads root. upload_subdir() rejects dot-only/dot-leading names and order_upload_dir() re-checks the resolved path stays inside UPLOADS_DIR; six traversal cases pinned in test_erasure_contract.py. A regex written for identifiers is not automatically safe as a filesystem name.
nodes.norm_label: order_id '..' matched the identifier regex — path segment needs its own check

nodes.label: _no_order/ bucket for direct partner API uploads
nodes.rationale: Direct-API uploads happen before any order exists, so they belong to no order; excluded from directory deletes and cleaned by the GC on age.
nodes.norm_label: _no_order/ bucket for direct partner api uploads

nodes.label: Product Editor PRD (End-to-End Production Automation, v1.13)
nodes.author: Kanna
nodes.norm_label: product editor prd (end-to-end production automation, v1.13)

nodes.label: Manual design preflight checkpoint (1-3 h per order, fixed-capacity team)
nodes.rationale: Exists because the legacy system had no customer preview and no automatic quality/quantity validation; stalls orders on customer response, misses the 3 PM courier cutoff, causes cancellations and cannot scale with volume.
nodes.norm_label: manual design preflight checkpoint (1-3 h per order, fixed-capacity team)

nodes.label: Target: under 5 minutes upload-to-production, zero human intervention
nodes.norm_label: target: under 5 minutes upload-to-production, zero human intervention

nodes.label: Track A: customer-facing preview and quantity validation before checkout
nodes.rationale: The customer self-validates by approving the preview; empty frames, auto-fill/pick-to-fill and the over-quantity modal replace the preflight count check.
nodes.norm_label: track a: customer-facing preview and quantity validation before checkout

nodes.label: Low-resolution (effective DPI < 150) warning, non-blocking
nodes.rationale: Replaces preflight's 'is this file good enough' judgement; informs but never refuses the order; the estimate mirrors the placement maths of both renderers (src/lib/dpi-utils.ts).

nodes.label: Track A2: post-checkout 300 DPI render delivered by signed webhook (primary) or polling download (fallback)
nodes.norm_label: track a2: post-checkout 300 dpi render delivered by signed webhook (primary) or polling download (fallback)

nodes.label: Standalone generator: no internal OMS push (push_to_production_estimator_task retired v1.9)
nodes.rationale: The embed webhook gives the storefront everything it needs to attach files to the order, and the storefront already talks to OMS via its own integration; OMS_PRODUCTION_ESTIMATOR_URL was removed and dashboard renders enqueue zero downstream tasks.
nodes.norm_label: standalone generator: no internal oms push (push_to_production_estimator_task retired v1.9)

nodes.label: CMYK / soft-proof / ICC pipeline removed in v1.8; colour handled invisibly via image_loader
nodes.rationale: Output is PNG (default) or PDF only; the promised CMYK colour-space warning never shipped. Instead services/image_loader.py colour-manages every upload ICC->sRGB so Display-P3 and AdobeRGB photos stop shifting in print without the customer knowing what a profile is.
nodes.norm_label: cmyk / soft-proof / icc pipeline removed in v1.8; colour handled invisibly via image_loader

nodes.label: B2: Celery + Redis async render queue (standard worker, retries, GC task)
nodes.rationale: Synchronous generation held a Gunicorn thread for the whole render and blocked concurrent orders at festival peaks; the API now answers 202 with a job id and status URL and the render happens in a worker pool.
nodes.norm_label: b2: celery + redis async render queue (standard worker, retries, gc task)

nodes.label: B1: two-layer canvas state persistence (editor_state JSON + IndexedDB File blobs keyed by orderId/fileId)
nodes.rationale: Files do not serialise, so each gets a UUID fileId and the raw blob goes to IndexedDB; auto-restore rehydrates originalFile so a refresh recovers the full editing context. Quota is per-origin, so very large jobs are best submitted in one session.
nodes.norm_label: b1: two-layer canvas state persistence (editor_state json + indexeddb file blobs keyed by orderid/fileid)

nodes.label: B4: server-side chunked upload + render for every Submit/Download (threshold removed v1.8)
nodes.rationale: Client-side Fabric rendering of >20 canvases caused timeouts, blank frames and crashes on low-RAM devices; a single unified server contract handles webhooks, large batches and resumable uploads identically.
nodes.norm_label: b4: server-side chunked upload + render for every submit/download (threshold removed v1.8)

nodes.label: B3: SKU-to-layout mapping built then removed 2026-09-04 (printo.in owns resolution)
nodes.rationale: printo.in resolves SKU -> layout itself and passes the layout name into the embed session, so a second mapping here was one more thing to keep in sync; it was never populated. Both smoke tests assert /api/sku-layouts/ returns 404.
nodes.norm_label: b3: sku-to-layout mapping built then removed 2026-09-04 (printo.in owns resolution)

nodes.label: API key bundle leak closed: NEXT_PUBLIC_DIRECT_API_KEY replaced by server-side internal proxy
nodes.rationale: The key was extractable from any browser's DevTools; all dashboard/editor calls now route through /api/internal/proxy gated by the NextAuth cookie, with INTERNAL_API_KEY server-only.
nodes.norm_label: api key bundle leak closed: next_public_direct_api_key replaced by server-side internal proxy

nodes.label: B7: storefront webhook consumer confirmed working (43 sessions, 45 ZIP fetches, order 576430; closed 2026-10-13)
nodes.norm_label: b7: storefront webhook consumer confirmed working (43 sessions, 45 zip fetches, order 576430; closed 2026-10-13)

nodes.label: Open: production readiness sign-off (Mohan) — fallback for print-quality issues preflight would have caught
nodes.norm_label: open: production readiness sign-off (mohan) — fallback for print-quality issues preflight would have caught

nodes.label: Success metrics (TAT, hold rate, cancellation, render success, memory, image size)
nodes.norm_label: success metrics (tat, hold rate, cancellation, render success, memory, image size)

nodes.label: v1.13.x theme: absence of a signal read as good news (empty APIRequest, GC tombstones, stale disk stats)
nodes.rationale: APIRequest.objects.count() read 0 forever because nothing wrote to it; is_deleted counts read 0 whether the GC ran or never; disk stats lifted from the last sweep are stale exactly when nothing sweeps. Each fix records the signal explicitly (audit middleware, gc_last_run.json, live disk block).
nodes.norm_label: v1.13.x theme: absence of a signal read as good news (empty apirequest, gc tombstones, stale disk stats)

nodes.label: Large File Split Plan
nodes.rationale: Two files (api/views.py at 4,500 lines, editor page.tsx at 5,558 lines) conflicted across concurrent sessions, could not be read in one pass, and hid long-range interactions such as the PR #166 autosave-overwrite bug. Done 2026-10-06..07.

nodes.label: Part 1: api/views.py -> api/views/ package
nodes.rationale: Three PRs (#189, #190, #191) split one 4,500-line module into system, ops, media, layouts, layout_admin, calendar_assets, render, downloads, embed, uploads; __init__.py only re-exports so urls.py, tests and management commands keep importing from api.views.

nodes.label: Part 2: editor page.tsx split into hooks and components
nodes.rationale: 13 split PRs (A, B1-B4, C1-C8) after a safety net, riskiest last (persistence C8 highest). page.tsx went 5,558 -> 622 lines; it keeps shared state, hook calls in original order, and markup.
nodes.norm_label: part 2: editor page.tsx split into hooks and components

nodes.label: views/_common.py shared constants module
nodes.rationale: Module-level constants shared across submodules (LAYOUT_ID_NOTE, OPS_WRITE_AUTH, UUID_GUARD) and the shared is_safe_layout_name guard live here; it imports nothing from the package because a submodule importing from api.views would be circular.

nodes.label: Move, don't change (split PR rule)
nodes.rationale: A split PR only relocates code with the same dependency arrays and no new eslint-disables; bugs or duplicates found along the way get their own PR so a regression points at one change.

nodes.label: Patch the submodule, not the api.views re-export
nodes.rationale: patch('api.views._write_holidays') stops intercepting once the view lives in api.views.calendar_assets because the re-export is a second reference; tests such as test_ops_write_routes.py and test_csp_report.py must target the submodule.
nodes.norm_label: patch the submodule, not the api.views re-export

nodes.label: Editor page Jest characterization suite (Phase 0a)
nodes.rationale: Renders the whole page under Jest/happy-dom against a FakeBackend that records requests in order and can hold a response back; every key test was proven able to fail by breaking the guarded rule in page.tsx (8 deliberate breaks). Must pass unchanged across every split PR.

nodes.label: Playwright editor smoke suite (Phase 0b)
nodes.rationale: Covers what Jest cannot run: a fake storefront page receiving pe:back / pe:render_job, the enforced frame-ancestors policy, a real server render to a ZIP, imposition, real image decoding including HEIC, a phone profile. Local only because GitHub Actions is billing-locked.

nodes.label: Detached download links fix
nodes.rationale: Three download helpers (handleQuickDownload, the dashboard ZIP hand-off in executeServerRender, downloadBlob in lib/zip-utils.ts) attached a temporary <a> to document.body; all now click a detached <a>, which every current browser can download from (PR #195).

nodes.label: Keep effect order when extracting hooks
nodes.rationale: Effects run in declaration order and some depend on it (latest-value ref mirrors), so a hook is called where its first effect used to be; the Escape handler sits after useImposition because it reads that state.
nodes.norm_label: keep effect order when extracting hooks

nodes.label: One owner per ref
nodes.rationale: A ref belongs to the hook that writes it; anything else receives it explicitly. duplicateFills and intentionalDupesRef stay in page.tsx because the memo reads the ref during render, which the React Compiler lint rejects outside that file.

nodes.label: Before/after proof for backend split PRs
nodes.rationale: OpenAPI schema byte-identical between main and branch, every api.views name still importable, URL patterns resolve to the same classes, all tests pass, and two live servers (pe-split:before / pe-split:after images on the compose network) answer the moved endpoints identically on one database.
nodes.norm_label: before/after proof for backend split prs

nodes.label: Deploy each split PR soon after merge
nodes.rationale: Decided 2026-10-07 so a regression points at one PR; C4-C8 deployed outside Indian business hours; rollback is git revert + ./deploy.sh.
nodes.norm_label: deploy each split pr soon after merge

nodes.label: Sticky toolbar pinning fix (B3 prerequisite)
nodes.rationale: The toolbar never pinned when scrolled: the IntersectionObserver was set up once, before the toolbar existed (it renders only after the layout loads), through a plain ref nothing re-ran. The sentinel is now held in state through a callback ref (PR #207).

nodes.label: AI Guardrails
nodes.rationale: Condensed list of rules that exist because breaking them already cost something; CLAUDE.md is the full reference and wins on disagreement. Last verified 2026-09-16 at fbebef3.

nodes.label: No AI image manipulation
nodes.rationale: Background removal, product detection and generative editing stay out; the one sanctioned ML feature is auto-orientation (MediaPipe Pose at POST /api/orientation/detect), which only reads the photo and persists nothing.

nodes.label: LayoutEngine must receive layout_definition from LayoutCatalogue
nodes.rationale: Missing layout_definition= causes [Errno 2] No such file or directory on render; LayoutEngine must never load layouts from disk itself. Four call sites were missing it in the 2026-09-04 audit.
nodes.norm_label: layoutengine must receive layout_definition from layoutcatalogue

nodes.label: Ops asset writes go through storage.write_calendar_asset
nodes.rationale: fonts.json, calendar_styles and holidays must be written via write_calendar_asset / delete_calendar_asset, never open() or os.remove(): local-disk writes are invisible to S3-backed deployments and lost on container restart. Atomic (temp + rename locally, single put on S3) and cache-invalidating.
nodes.norm_label: ops asset writes go through storage.write_calendar_asset

nodes.label: self.retry() only, never autoretry_for
nodes.rationale: Keeps the DB retry_count and Celery's internal counter in sync. Exponential backoff (2**n)*2 -> 2s, 4s, 8s; MemoryError and SoftTimeLimitExceeded skip retries and fail the job immediately.

nodes.label: Caller webhook is a separate Celery task
nodes.rationale: notify_caller_webhook_task must not block the render worker slot and retries independently up to 5x; callback_url is stored on CanvasData at submission (from EmbedSession via X-Callback-URL), not passed through the task chain. Only dispatched when canvas.callback_url is set.
nodes.norm_label: caller webhook is a separate celery task

nodes.label: Dispatch Celery tasks inside transaction.on_commit
nodes.rationale: Dispatch lives in RenderSubmissionService (api/render_submission.py), shared by both render views. A Redis failure on dispatch must set RenderJob.status='failed' with the error rather than leave the job silently queued.

nodes.label: priority queue has no producer and is not a QoS tier
nodes.rationale: One worker (celery-worker-standard) consumes -Q priority,standard as a safety net so an opt-in apply_async(queue='priority') cannot sit in Redis forever. Celery round-robins across -Q queues, so naming priority first buys no precedence; the second worker was removed Aug 2026 having never executed a task.
nodes.norm_label: priority queue has no producer and is not a qos tier

nodes.label: Poison-pill guard counts only broker redeliveries
nodes.rationale: render_canvas_task aborts after 3 crash-redeliveries detected via delivery_info.redelivered. A worker crash under acks_late redelivers the SAME message (redelivered=True, retries frozen); self.retry() publishes a NEW one. Conflating them would abort healthy jobs.
nodes.norm_label: poison-pill guard counts only broker redeliveries

nodes.label: Caller-facing layout lookups go through LayoutCatalogue.resolve_active
nodes.rationale: resolve_active walks the multi-hop, cycle-guarded renamed_to chain so a pre-2026-09-16 rename keeps resolving. GetLayoutView, ExternalLayoutDetailView, EditorInitView, the qty-policy lookup, GenerateLayoutView and render_canvas_task all use it; ops-only LayoutManagementView.get stays literal because ops needs exact identity including deprecated rows.
nodes.norm_label: caller-facing layout lookups go through layoutcatalogue.resolve_active

nodes.label: Layout rename retired; display_name is the editable field
nodes.rationale: A rename broke printo.in's embed on 2026-09-16 because their iframe URL hardcodes the layout name. POST /api/ops/layouts/<name> now 400s if old_name differs from name and LayoutCatalogue.save() raises ValueError if .name changes on an existing row.
nodes.norm_label: layout rename retired; display_name is the editable field

nodes.label: Omitting display_name on save must not blank it
nodes.rationale: LayoutManagementView.post only overwrites display_name when the request carries a non-empty value, falling back to default_display_name_for(name) only on first create, because not every ops surface sends it on every save.
nodes.norm_label: omitting display_name on save must not blank it

nodes.label: Embed proxy allowlist is path AND method
nodes.rationale: Prefix-only until 2026-09-03: fonts, holidays and calendar-styles accept ops writes upstream and the proxy injects the session's real (ops-flagged DIRECT) api_key, so an embed token could PUT holiday data. ALLOWED_PATH_METHODS names the verbs per prefix.
nodes.norm_label: embed proxy allowlist is path and method

nodes.label: Ops-tier gate must cover dual-mounted write views
nodes.rationale: CalendarStylesView and HolidaysView serve public paths and ops/ twins; their write handlers never check the route and every internal-proxy request carries the ops-flagged INTERNAL_API_KEY. Closed twice on 2026-09-29: OPS_OWNED_PATHS in requiresOpsTier, and api/urls.py mounts the public routes READ_ONLY (405).
nodes.norm_label: ops-tier gate must cover dual-mounted write views

nodes.label: Never git reset --hard or checkout -- storage/ on prod
nodes.rationale: storage/layouts, masks and fonts.json were git-tracked and rewritten by the ops UI; prod diverged (20 tracked layouts deleted, 11 untracked replacements). Either command resurrects the obsolete catalogue beside the live one so a customer can open the wrong product.
nodes.norm_label: never git reset --hard or checkout -- storage/ on prod

nodes.label: Don't raise DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE for autosave
nodes.rationale: 37% of autosaves 400'd because editor_state embedded base64 previews averaging 16 MB. Raising the limit would make gunicorn buffer those per request on a 2-core box with a 2 GB worker cap, trading silent save failures for OOM; shrink the payload instead (done in PR #134).

nodes.label: Every autosave goes through scheduleAutosave gated on restoreSettled
nodes.rationale: Autosave writes empty state on purpose, so a PUT before the restore GET lands wipes the saved design. The 2026-08-09 restorePending guard keyed on ?order_id= which the embed iframe never has, and the calendar/book writers skipped it (fixed PR #166). Don't PUT canvas-state from anywhere else.
nodes.norm_label: every autosave goes through scheduleautosave gated on restoresettled

nodes.label: Every handler needs @extend_schema with request= and responses=
nodes.rationale: drf-spectacular drops an undecorated handler from the reference. SECURITY_DEFINITIONS is a drf-yasg key silently ignored; auth schemes live in api/schema.py as OpenApiAuthenticationExtension subclasses registered from ApiConfig.ready(). FontsView/CalendarStylesView/HolidaysView are AllowAny with inline ops checks so every operation must set auth= explicitly. Validate with manage.py spectacular --validate --fail-on-warn.
nodes.norm_label: every handler needs @extend_schema with request= and responses=

nodes.label: Qty enforcement is deliberately asymmetric
nodes.rationale: Hard cap going over (Keep first N / Choose again in the editor, 400 from EditorRenderView), warn-and-proceed going under on both sides. qty is caller-supplied so a wrong value must not strand a real order; qty_violation has one > and no lower bound. Server half is narrower (exempts calendars and books) and fails open.

nodes.label: Submit-time qty cap reads EmbedSession, not X-Order-Qty
nodes.rationale: A caller holding the real api_key can POST /api/editor/render directly with no proxy, so the header never arrives (reproduced 2026-09-15: qty=5, 7 files, 202). EditorRenderView looks EmbedSession.qty up by (order_id, api_key). Legacy ?qty=N is UI-only. Anything the proxy injects as a header must also be in its cached tuple.
nodes.norm_label: submit-time qty cap reads embedsession, not x-order-qty

nodes.label: Add Files appends, never replaces
nodes.rationale: A native <input type=file> pick contains only that pick's files; handleFileChange must merge onto the existing selection or every earlier canvas is wiped (live bug until PR #24). Multi-surface layouts are excluded since each surface holds one photo.

nodes.label: Low-res DPI warning stays non-blocking and mirrors placement maths
nodes.rationale: src/lib/dpi-utils.ts (DPI_WARN=150, DPI_CRITICAL=100, strict <) mirrors fabric-renderer.ts and engine.py exactly; change placement maths in either renderer and update dpi-utils too or the warning lies.
nodes.norm_label: low-res dpi warning stays non-blocking and mirrors placement maths

nodes.label: No CMYK / ICC soft-proof pipeline
nodes.rationale: Removed in v1.8 (cmyk.py, icc_profiles/, _generate_soft_proof_for_surface, CanvasData.soft_proof). Colour is handled invisibly by services/image_loader.py (ICC->sRGB at load, sRGB-tagged output); never Image.open(...).convert('RGBA') a customer photo directly.

nodes.label: Don't cross editor_state and render_state
nodes.rationale: Post-0008: editor_state is frontend-owned (CanvasStateView autosave only); render_state is pipeline-owned (EditorRenderView at submit only). As one field the two writers clobbered each other: submit wiped the autosaved design and a post-submit autosave could strip a queued job's payload.

nodes.label: CanvasStateView.put keeps image_paths out of update_or_create defaults
nodes.rationale: Writing image_paths or [] in defaults blanked recorded paths every 2 s, so DPDP erasure reported files_deleted: 0 while photos stayed on disk (migration 0011). The column carries default=list (0013) so INSERT works; a model default applies on INSERT only.
nodes.norm_label: canvasstateview.put keeps image_paths out of update_or_create defaults

nodes.label: CanvasData is always upserted by order_id
nodes.rationale: update_or_create(order_id=..., defaults={...}), never create(), so operator retries and customer resubmissions don't hit a unique-constraint error. celery_task_id is nullable and set after enqueue, never ''.
nodes.norm_label: canvasdata is always upserted by order_id

nodes.label: isExport flag gates preview-only overlays
nodes.rationale: Frame outlines and preview overlays render only when !isExport; both FabricEditor.tsx and fabric-renderer.ts must respect it or they appear in downloads.

nodes.label: Storage Migration Technical Design (Kiro spec)
nodes.rationale: Low-level design for moving layouts from git-tracked JSON into Postgres LayoutCatalogue and masks/calendar assets into S3, organised by implementation phase (model+0016, S3Storage, view refactor, masks, asset_store, gitignore). Written before PR #111; the shipped code diverged in places (rename later retired, calendar-asset fallback replaced by CalendarAssetUnavailable, masks under a prefix).

nodes.label: LayoutCatalogue model design
nodes.rationale: name (unique, case-sensitive) is the identifier and overrides definition['name']; definition JSONField; product_type inferred at import; is_deprecated soft delete; version bumped per write; imported_at/imported_by co-validated in clean(). A separate LayoutPermission table was deferred because APIKey.can_list_layouts suffices.

nodes.label: Migration 0016_import_layout_catalogue
